prompt: A pool holds $180$ gallons. How many quarts is that? ($1$ gal $= 4$ qt)
hint: Every gallon in the pool is worth the same number of quarts. Quarts are smaller, so the count will go up.

hints.title: 🔁 Another angle
hints.text: Start with a small pool: how many quarts are in $2$ gallons? Decide whether the number of quarts is bigger or smaller than the number of gallons.
Every gallon in the pool is worth the same number of quarts. Quarts are smaller, so the count will go up.
Multiply the $180$ gallons by $4$ quarts per gallon. Splitting it as $100 \times 4$ and $80 \times 4$ makes it easier.

explanation: Each gallon equals $4$ quarts, so the number of quarts is the gallons times $4$.
Break $180$ into $100 + 80$ to multiply in parts: $100 \times 4 = 400$ and $80 \times 4 = 320$.
Add the two partial products to get the total: $400 + 320 = 720$.
The pool holds $720$ quarts of water.
